_claudeMdNote: CLAUDE.md is gitignored, so the ship gate's usual consistency grep could never see version drift inside it — and this repo's copy claimed 0.14.7 while the app shipped 0.14.10, three releases stale, until v0.14.11. The pattern above deliberately matches ONLY the `- **Version**: X.Y.Z` declaration line. Historical prose that names an old version ('v0.14.7 adopted Node 24 LTS') is correct as written and must not be flagged. The check is skipped in CI, where the file is never checked out.

commands.name: lint
commands._note: Accepted baseline, MEASURED 2026-08-22 on this committed config at v0.15.5 — never from a probe config. That is the recorded Story Map failure: a throwaway config omitting this repo's own no-unused-vars overrides reported 70 findings / 33 production when the truth was 22 / 8, and the owner chose on wrong numbers. COMPOSITION: all 10 are sonarjs/cognitive-complexity errors — 0 warnings, 0 from any other rule, 0 in test files. NINE sit in COVERED files (csv.ts 97.56%, import-utils.ts 98.71%, invitation-errors.ts 100%, storage.ts 76.38%, auth-context.tsx 1.56%); exactly ONE is in a zero-coverage file, use-grid-navigation.ts. Worst is storage.ts:147 validateProjectData at cc 35. RATCHET, NOT REMEDIATION: accepted, not owed. TOOLING-ROLLOUT 9.1 — installing the checker sets a number you hold steady, not a debt to clear. Zero is not the goal; scheduler ran at 23 for months and closed at 3, all three informed declines. Complexity ranks COST OF CHANGE, not probability of defect: scheduler shipped six user-visible defects and the metric found none of them. TWO THINGS THIS KEY CHANGES, both read in scripts/shipgate.mjs lines 329-345. (1) The count is ESLint's ALL-RULE problem total, not a complexity count. It is all complexity today only because the repo otherwise lints clean; the day one unrelated warning appears, this gate fails with a message about baselines that names complexity nowhere. (2) Setting this key DISABLES exit-code gating for the lint step: that branch ends in `continue`, so the `exitCode === 0` check never runs. Before, any lint error failed the gate. After, a lint error passes if the total is unchanged — fix one finding and add one unused-var error in the same PR and this goes green. The trade is deliberate and it is NOT strictly stronger. If the count ever reaches 0, DELETE this key rather than setting it to 0: ESLint prints no problem line at all, so the gate reads null and fails saying it could not read a problem count, naming neither complexity nor the fix. Measured on this repo before the install.

commands.name: typecheck
commands._note: Deliberately separate from `build`, and NOT redundant with it — do not delete this step on the assumption that `next build` already covers types. It does not cover test files. Next builds the TS program from the full tsconfig `fileNames`, test files included, then discards every diagnostic whose path matches `__tests__/`|`__mocks__/` or `*.test.*`|`*.spec.*` (next/dist/lib/typescript/runTypeCheck.js, Next 16.2.9). The exclusion is by FILENAME and unconditional — importing a test file into the app would NOT bring it under the build. Every test file here matches both patterns, twice over — derive the set with `git ls-files ':(glob)src/**/*.test.*'`, never store a count. `tsc --noEmit` covers them because tsconfig includes `**/*.ts`. MEASURED 2026-08-17 with `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors, so this gate went in at zero with no baseline to accept. FALSIFIED in the install commit (v0.15.0) rather than assumed: a TS2322 (`const x: number = <string>`) injected into src/lib/__tests__/colors.test.ts drove THIS step red — `colors.test.ts(41,7): error TS2322` — while `build (next build)` passed GREEN in the SAME run, which is the coverage gap demonstrated rather than argued; lint and test were inert to the probe; probe reverted and md5-asserted byte-identical. Sibling context: GanttApp has carried three TS2802 errors in test files since 2026-07-30 (c4e174a — the very commit that added its ship gate), green on every gate step since, because it has no step like this one. cfd was clean only by CIRCUMSTANCE: identical exposure, spared GanttApp's specific error class only by `target: ES2017` rather than es5. THE RULE: a note asserting X must name the COMMAND that measured X.

commands.name: build (next build)
commands._note: `next build` typechecks production source and is a real gate for it — `next.config.ts` sets no `ignoreBuildErrors`. It does NOT gate test files, and not because they are unimported: Next builds the program from the full tsconfig `fileNames`, test files included, then discards every diagnostic whose path matches `__tests__/`|`__mocks__/` or `*.test.*`|`*.spec.*` (next/dist/lib/typescript/runTypeCheck.js, Next 16.2.9). Every test file here matches both patterns, so no import arrangement brings them under the build. `npm run typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit`, tsconfig `include: **/*.ts` — is the command that covers them. This REPLACES a note reading '`next build` runs tsc, so types are covered by the build here — unlike the Vite repos, which needed tsc wired in explicitly', which was false; its contrast with the Vite repos gave it the authority of a considered finding, and it is precisely what would have justified deleting the typecheck step as redundant. The step name also dropped its '— typechecks' suffix, which carried the same overclaim. Shown false by measurement in the v0.15.0 install commit — see the typecheck step's note.
